questions.question: Q: What type of chart would you use to compare the favourite subjects of boys and girls in a school?
questions.correctAnswer: A dual (comparative) bar chart, because it shows two groups side by side for each category, making comparison easy.

questions.question: Q: From a cumulative frequency curve, the total frequency is 80. At what cumulative frequency value do you read the lower quartile?
questions.correctAnswer: Lower quartile is at 25% of total: 0.25 × 80 = 20. Read the value on the x-axis at cumulative frequency 20.

questions.question: Q: Points on a scatter graph generally rise from bottom-left to top-right. What type of correlation does this suggest?
questions.correctAnswer: This suggests a positive correlation — as one variable increases, the other also tends to increase.

questions.question: Q: How do you plot a frequency polygon for a grouped frequency table?
questions.correctAnswer: Plot the midpoint of each class interval on the x-axis against its frequency on the y-axis, then join the points with straight lines.

questions.question: Q: What is the key difference between a bar chart and a histogram?
questions.correctAnswer: A bar chart has gaps between bars and is used for discrete/qualitative data; a histogram has no gaps and is used for continuous data, with bar area proportional to frequency.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response The grouped frequency table shows the marks of 40 students in a test. Draw a cumulative frequency curve and use it to find the median and interquartile range. 0–20: 4, 20–40: 8, 40–60: 16, 60–80: 8, 80–100: 4 <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: Plot cumulative frequencies at upper class boundaries: 20: 4, 40: 12, 60: 28, 80: 36, 100: 40 Draw a smooth S-shaped curve through the points. Median at cumulative frequency = 40 ÷ 2 = 20: Read from 20 on the y-axis → approximately 50 on the x-axis. Lower quartile at cumulative frequency = 40 ÷ 4 = 10: Read from 10 → approximately 35. Upper quartile at cumulative frequency = 3 × 40 ÷ 4 = 30: Read from 30 → approximately 65. Interquartile range = 65 – 35 = 30 marks.
